name: berth-plugin-incus
description: Virtual machines and containers on an Incus server for berth hosts.

provisioners.label: Incus virtual machine
provisioners.description: A KVM guest on an Incus server, set up from berth's cloud seed. The server needs KVM.

arguments.name: server
arguments.label: Incus server
arguments.help: The address of the Incus server's API, such as https://192.0.2.10:8443.

arguments.name: project
arguments.label: Project
arguments.help: The Incus project berth makes its machines in and looks at.

arguments.name: cpus
arguments.label: CPUs
arguments.help: How many CPUs the virtual machine gets.

arguments.name: memory
arguments.label: Memory
arguments.help: How much memory it gets, such as 8GiB.

arguments.name: disk
arguments.label: Disk size
arguments.help: The size of its root disk, such as 60GiB.

arguments.name: image
arguments.label: Image
arguments.help: The image on images.linuxcontainers.org to start from. It has to have cloud-init.

arguments.name: pool
arguments.label: Storage pool
arguments.help: The storage pool of the Incus server its disk is in.

arguments.name: network
arguments.label: Network
arguments.help: The network it is attached to. Empty takes the network of the default profile.

arguments.name: image
arguments.label: Image
arguments.help: The image on images.linuxcontainers.org to start from, such as debian/12 or alpine/3.20. It becomes no berth host: nothing of berth is put in it.

arguments.name: user_data
arguments.label: Cloud-init user data
arguments.help: What cloud-init does on its first boot, such as packages to install and users to add, for an image that has cloud-init. Empty leaves the image as it is.

arguments.name: cpus
arguments.label: CPUs
arguments.help: How many CPUs the virtual machine gets.

arguments.name: memory
arguments.label: Memory
arguments.help: How much memory it gets, such as 2GiB.

arguments.name: disk
arguments.label: Disk size
arguments.help: The size of its root disk, such as 20GiB.

arguments.name: pool
arguments.label: Storage pool
arguments.help: The storage pool of the Incus server its disk is in.

arguments.name: network
arguments.label: Network
arguments.help: The network it is attached to. Empty takes the network of the default profile.

actions.name: server
actions.label: Check the server
actions.help: Ask the Incus server for its version, its kernel and its storage drivers, and whether it trusts berth's client certificate.

actions.name: pools
actions.label: Storage pools
actions.help: The storage pools of the server, with how much of each is used.

actions.name: images
actions.label: Cached images
actions.help: The images the server keeps in its project, with their sizes. Incus fetches one from images.linuxcontainers.org when a machine first needs it.

actions.name: networks
actions.label: Networks
actions.help: The networks of the server a machine can be attached to.

actions.name: volumes
actions.label: Volumes
actions.help: The custom volumes of every storage pool in the project, with their sizes and whether an instance uses each.

actions.name: create-volume
actions.label: New volume
actions.help: Create a custom volume in a storage pool, which an instance can mount.

arguments.name: pool
arguments.label: Pool
arguments.help: The storage pool to create it in.

arguments.name: name
arguments.label: Name
arguments.help: The name of the volume, such as wiki-data.

arguments.name: size
arguments.label: Size
arguments.help: The largest the volume may grow, such as 10GiB. Empty leaves it to the pool.

actions.name: remove-volume
actions.label: Remove volume
actions.confirm: Remove this volume and everything in it?
actions.help: Remove a custom volume and what is in it. Incus refuses it while an instance uses it.

arguments.name: pool
arguments.label: Pool
arguments.help: The storage pool it is in.

arguments.name: name
arguments.label: Name
arguments.help: The name of the volume to remove.

actions.name: create-pool
actions.label: New storage pool
actions.help: Create a storage pool on the server, for machines, instances and volumes.

arguments.name: name
arguments.label: Name
arguments.help: The name of the pool, such as fast.

arguments.name: driver
arguments.label: Driver
arguments.help: How the pool keeps its data. dir uses a folder on the server; the others make a loop file of the given size unless the server is set up otherwise.

arguments.name: size
arguments.label: Size
arguments.help: The size of the loop file for zfs, btrfs and lvm, such as 50GiB. dir takes no size.

actions.name: remove-pool
actions.label: Remove storage pool
actions.help: Remove a storage pool. Incus refuses it while it holds instances, volumes or images.

arguments.name: name
arguments.label: Name
arguments.help: The name of the pool to remove.

actions.name: remove-image
actions.label: Remove image
actions.confirm: Remove this image from the server?
actions.help: Remove a cached image from the project. Incus fetches it again when something needs it.

arguments.name: image
arguments.label: Image
arguments.help: The image's alias, or the start of its fingerprint as the cached images show it.

provisioners.label: Incus container
provisioners.description: A system container on an Incus server, set up from berth's cloud seed. Nesting is turned on so that the guest's systemd comes up.

arguments.name: server
arguments.label: Incus server
arguments.help: The address of the Incus server's API, such as https://192.0.2.10:8443.

arguments.name: project
arguments.label: Project
arguments.help: The Incus project berth makes its machines in and looks at.

arguments.name: cpus
arguments.label: CPUs
arguments.help: How many CPUs the container may use.

arguments.name: memory
arguments.label: Memory
arguments.help: How much memory it may use, such as 8GiB.

arguments.name: disk
arguments.label: Disk size
arguments.help: The size of its root disk, such as 60GiB.

arguments.name: image
arguments.label: Image
arguments.help: The image on images.linuxcontainers.org to start from. It has to have cloud-init.

arguments.name: pool
arguments.label: Storage pool
arguments.help: The storage pool of the Incus server its disk is in.

arguments.name: network
arguments.label: Network
arguments.help: The network it is attached to. Empty takes the network of the default profile.

arguments.name: image
arguments.label: Image
arguments.help: The image on images.linuxcontainers.org to start from, such as debian/12 or alpine/3.20. It becomes no berth host: nothing of berth is put in it.

arguments.name: user_data
arguments.label: Cloud-init user data
arguments.help: What cloud-init does on its first boot, such as packages to install and users to add, for an image that has cloud-init. Empty leaves the image as it is.

arguments.name: cpus
arguments.label: CPUs
arguments.help: How many CPUs the container gets.

arguments.name: memory
arguments.label: Memory
arguments.help: How much memory it gets, such as 2GiB.

arguments.name: disk
arguments.label: Disk size
arguments.help: The size of its root disk, such as 20GiB.

arguments.name: pool
arguments.label: Storage pool
arguments.help: The storage pool of the Incus server its disk is in.

arguments.name: network
arguments.label: Network
arguments.help: The network it is attached to. Empty takes the network of the default profile.

arguments.name: nesting
arguments.label: Nesting
arguments.help: Whether containers can run in it, such as Docker's. yes also lets the guest's systemd come up in an unprivileged container.
